And now our weekly look at getting to the airport. We compared the three usual ways, and the results are not what most people expect. The train is by far the cheapest, at about a quarter of the price of a taxi, and on a normal weekday morning it is also the fastest. The bus is slightly cheaper than the train, but it is much slower and far less reliable, because it sits in the same traffic as everybody else. The taxi is the most convenient of the three, because it takes you from your door to the terminal with no walking at all, and it is by far the most expensive. Our conclusion is simple. If you are travelling alone with one bag, take the train. If you are three people with heavy luggage, the taxi is better value for money than it looks.

Hello, this is Nina calling about the two hotels. I have looked at both of them and I want to give you my honest opinion before you make up your mind. The first one is closer to the office, about ten minutes on foot, and the rooms are bigger. It is also considerably more expensive, and I think it is slightly overpriced for what it offers. The second one is thirty minutes away by train, the rooms are smaller, but it is much quieter and the breakfast is far better. The downside of the second one is the journey in the morning. So: the first is more convenient, the second is better value for money. Call me back and tell me which one you want.

Nina asks Janderson whether he has made up his mind about the two hotels. He answers that he has not, and that he wants to compare them one more time. Nina says the first hotel is more convenient but slightly overpriced. Janderson replies that the second one looks like better value for money, even with the longer journey. Nina agrees and tells him the only real downside is the train in the morning.
